     def test_reversed_or(self):
         with self.assertRaisesMessage(NotImplementedError, self.bitwise_msg):
             object() | Combinable()
+
+    def test_order_by_multiline_sql(self):
+        # Test that multiline RawSQL in order_by doesn't get incorrectly deduplicated
+        # This tests the fix for the issue where multiline RawSQL expressions
+        # with identical last lines were being treated as duplicates
+        from django.db.models.expressions import RawSQL
+        
+        # Create a queryset with multiple multiline RawSQL order_by clauses
+        qs = Company.objects.all().order_by(
+            RawSQL('''
+                case when num_employees > 100
+                     then 2 else 1 end''', []).desc(),
+            RawSQL('''
+                case when num_employees > 100
+                     then num_chairs
+                     else null end''', []).asc(),
+            RawSQL('''
+                case when num_employees < 100
+                     then num_chairs
+                     else null end''', []).desc())
+        
+        # The query should include all three order_by clauses
+        # If the bug exists, the second and third clauses would be removed
+        # because their last lines are identical
+        query_str = str(qs.query)
+        
+        # Count how many times we see the pattern "else null end" in the query
+        # We should see it at least twice (from the second and third RawSQL)
+        count = query_str.count('else null end')
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(count, 2, 
+            "Multiline RawSQL order_by clauses are being incorrectly deduplicated")
